summary: This roadmap extends the potential-automorphy infrastructure to crystalline weight-zero lifts over CM and totally real fields with p arbitrarily ramified. It assembles the adequate-image Taylor–Wiles arithmetic tower, geometric local-component comparison, nilpotent derived Hecke actions and solvable preparation needed for the weight-zero lifting theorem, and exports the adequate ordinary companion. Local compatibility, crystalline generic reducedness, connects and abstract patching retain their existing owners.

nodes.title: Prepared weight-zero lifting data
nodes.statement: Fix an imaginary CM field F with maximal totally real subfield F⁺ and conjugation c, n≥1, an odd prime p>n, ι:Q̄_p≅C, and a regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL_n(A_F) of weight zero. PreparedWeightZeroData consists of finite S containing S_p and R⊂S\S_p, with A=S\(R∪S_p), and the following certificates. Every rational prime below S or ramified in F splits in some imaginary quadratic subfield of F. For each p-place v̄ of F⁺ there is another v̄′ above p such that the sum of [F⁺_w:Q_p] over w above p different from both is strictly greater than [F⁺:Q]/2. The residual r̄_ι(π) is absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic, and its restriction to G_{F(ζ_p)} has adequate image. π is unramified at S_p and outside S. At v∈R, π_v has Iwahori fixed vectors, q_v≡1 modulo p and r̄_v is trivial. At v∈A, π_v is unramified, v∉R^c and H²(F_v,ad r̄)=0. A contains two places of different residue characteristics. Enlarge the finite p-adic coefficient field E to contain the Galois closure of F, the residual values, ζ_p, all auxiliary characters and fields of definition of geometric local components. Its ring of integers is O, uniformizer ϖ and residue field k. Neither a polarization nor a fixed determinant is part of these data.
proofSteps: Take the eight arithmetic conditions as separate fields with their actual mathematical meanings; their conjunction is a reusable profile, not a replacement for the supplier definitions of adequacy or decomposed genericity.
Use CN Theorem 4.3.1 to identify the seed local representations as crystalline with weights {0,…,n−1}. Coefficient extension is allowed before fixing universal rings.
acceptance: An absolutely ramified p is allowed.
The complementary degree sum uses a global degree over Q.
Pairwise distinct residual Frobenius eigenvalues are not substituted for decomposed genericity.

nodes.title: Prepared local level factors
nodes.statement: For the prepared profile, construct K=∏_v K_v inside GL_n(A_F,f), with K_v=GL_n(O_{F_v}) for v∉S or v∈S_p, K_v=Iw_v for v∈R, and K_v=Iw_{v,1} for v∈A. Here Iw is the preimage of the upper triangular Borel under reduction and Iw_{v,1} is its pro-residue-characteristic Iwahori radical, the preimage of the upper unipotent subgroup. These are supplier compact-open groups. The algebraic interface LevelFactors selects among three supplied subgroup families using S,S_p,R; the arithmetic specialization proves compactness, openness, factorization and neatness of their adelic product, and π^K≠0. The two auxiliary residue characteristics ensure neatness; no assertion that a single pro-v factor always suffices is made.
proofSteps: Select the hyperspecial branch first, then the R branch, then the auxiliary branch; the partition prevents conflicting local conditions.
Form the adelic compact-open product using ALS.1. At R use Iwahori invariants and at A use unramified seed vectors. Apply the two-prime neatness argument of ACC Lemma 6.5.2.
acceptance: S_p always has hyperspecial level.
A has pro-v Iwahori, not full Iwahori.
K is good in the geometric supplier sense.

nodes.title: Inverse auxiliary character coefficients
nodes.statement: Given a finite index set I, groups G_i, a group H, a commutative coefficient ring O, characters χ_i:G_i→Oˣ and a homomorphism θ:H→∏_i G_i, define AuxiliaryCoefficient(χ,θ) to be the representation on the existing O-module O in which h acts on x by (∏_i χ_i(θ(h)_i))⁻¹x. In the arithmetic specialization I consists of pairs (v,i) with v∈R and 1≤i≤n, G_(v,i)=k(v)ˣ, H=K_S and θ is the diagonal reduction of the Iwahori factors, trivial on the other factors. The characters reduce to one modulo ϖ. Require either the entire tuple to be trivial, or the characters at each v∈R to be pairwise distinct; independent choices of these two alternatives at different places are not the stated profile. This definition is the proof-specific coefficient O(χ⁻¹), reusing Mathlib Representation and the scalar module O; it is not a new theory of one-dimensional representations.
proofSteps: Compose the product character with θ, invert it, and let its units act by scalar multiplication as O-linear endomorphisms.
The character and scalar-action laws supply the representation laws. Reduction of every χ_i to one makes the entire residual coefficient action trivial, with the identity on O/ϖ as comparison map.
acceptance: The inverse is essential: a character value 2 acts on 1 by 1/2.
An empty R produces the trivial coefficient.
Reduction has a specified comparison, not merely an isomorphism class.

nodes.title: Weight-zero variable-determinant deformation problem
nodes.statement: For the prepared profile and an allowed χ tuple, instantiate the imported variable-determinant global problem S_χ=(r̄,S,{O},{D_v}). At v∈S_p choose the framed crystalline quotient with HT_τ={0,…,n−1}; at v∈R use D_v^χ, whose characteristic polynomial on inertia is ∏_{i=1}^n(X−χ_{v,i}(Art_v⁻¹σ)); at v∈A use the full framed lifting functor. D_v^χ uses the character of k(v)ˣ inflated to O_{F_v}ˣ and geometric local Artin reciprocity. The associated unframed ring R_{S_χ}, S-framed ring R^S_{S_χ}, and local base R_loc^χ=completed tensor over O of all R_v are the supplier representing objects, with chosen universal representatives. Write R_p for the completed tensor of the crystalline p-factors, the same for χ and 1. Provide the residual identifications R_loc^χ/ϖ≅R_loc^1/ϖ and R_{S_χ}/ϖ≅R_{S_1}/ϖ, compatible with the chosen residual universal representations. No determinant is imposed and the framing count is n²|S|−1.
proofSteps: Insert the three local conditions in the G8 functor, using the crystalline point criterion and the tame characteristic-polynomial quotient.

Use G8 representability and its chosen S-framing comparison. Away from p, the χ and trivial characteristic-polynomial ideals agree modulo ϖ; extend through completed tensor products and global representing functors.

nodes.title: Weight-zero deformation-to-Hecke surjection
nodes.statement: For S_χ and O(χ⁻¹) above, let T_χ be the localized derived spherical Hecke image on RΓ(X_K,O(χ⁻¹)) at the non-Eisenstein ideal m attached to r̄. There is δ≥1 depending only on n and [F:Q], an ideal J_χ of T_χ with J_χ^δ=0, and a continuous surjection of local O-algebras f_χ:R_{S_χ}→T_χ/J_χ. For every v∉S the universal representation after applying f_χ has geometric-Frobenius polynomial P_v(X)=Σ_{i=0}^n(−1)^i q_v^{i(i−1)/2}T_{v,i}X^{n−i}, T_{v,0}=1. The quotient is essential. Via Spec(T_χ/J_χ)≅Spec T_χ and Spec pullback along f_χ, the union of the supports of its cohomology groups is a well-defined closed subset of Spec R_{S_χ}; it does not require a genuine R_{S_χ}-module chain action.
proofSteps: Use CN CL.7 at each p-place with T=S∪S^c, weight zero and the crystalline parabolic branch. The prepared splitting conditions verify the extra ramified-prime hypothesis for T, and the strict degree bound implies CN’s weak bound.

Combine the local crystalline factorizations with the tame and unrestricted conditions of ACC Proposition 6.5.3. Enlarge the nilpotent error ideal by the finite sum/product bounds, retaining a bound depending only on n and the global degree.
Construct the universal deformation map, prove surjectivity from Frobenius Hecke coefficients, then use the nilpotent spectral identification to transport support.
acceptance: δ does not depend on χ, coefficient exponent or Taylor–Wiles depth.
For n=1 the polynomial is X−T_{v,1}; for n=3 its last coefficient is negative.
No integral R=T assertion or lift through J_χ is inferred.

nodes.title: Cuspidal recognition of characteristic-zero support
nodes.statement: At the good prepared GL_n level with trivial coefficients, a characteristic-zero Hecke eigensystem in H*(X_K,E)_m, with the specified absolutely irreducible residual system, is realized by a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation Π of weight zero with Π^K≠0. Conversely the prepared seed π supplies a nonzero such eigensystem and the associated O-valued deformation point after finite coefficient extension. Comparing geometric-Frobenius polynomials identifies the attached semisimple Galois representation with a given lift represented by that eigensystem. The ordinary cohomology comparison must exclude the noncuspidal summands using the residual irreducibility hypothesis; the inclusion of cuspidal cohomology alone is insufficient.
proofSteps: Use the Betti-to-automorphic comparison and the residual non-Eisenstein cuspidality consequence of ACC Theorem 2.4.10.

Read weight zero from the trivial coefficient infinitesimal character and K-fixed vectors from the finite automorphic factor. Use characteristic-zero Galois attachment and Frobenius uniqueness for identification.
acceptance: A seed π with π^K≠0 produces nonzero rational cohomology.

nodes.title: Dimension and characteristic of local tensor components
nodes.statement: For either the all-trivial χ tuple or one pairwise distinct at every R-place, R_loc^χ is O-flat and equidimensional, of Krull dimension D=1+n²|S|+n(n−1)[F:Q]/2; every irreducible component has a characteristic-zero generic point. All local quotients used here are nonzero: the seed gives crystalline points, the trivial residual tame problems have lifts of the specified types, and the auxiliary unrestricted factors are formally smooth. After finite coefficient enlargement so their components and special-fibre components are geometrically irreducible, completed tensor components are indexed by products of local components. For a subset T⊂S the relative dimensions sum with a single coefficient dimension, rather than adding |T| copies of the O-dimension.
proofSteps: Use crystalline flatness and dimension 1+n²+n(n−1)[F_v:Q_p]/2 at p; each R- and A-factor has dimension 1+n².
Apply the geometrically irreducible completed-tensor component and dimension theorem of BLGHT Lemma 3.3 and ACC Lemma 6.2.25. Sum local p-degrees to [F:Q], keeping one O-dimension.
acceptance: For n=2 and [F:Q]=2, D=3+4|S|.

nodes.title: Unique generic generalization from the special fibre
nodes.statement: Every generic point of Spec(R_loc^χ/ϖ) is the specialization of exactly one generic point of Spec R_loc^χ. At a p-factor, apply the sibling weight-zero generic-reducedness theorem for p>n and the generic commutative-algebra bridge: at a special-fibre minimal prime, O-flatness and generic reducedness make the localized ring a one-dimensional regular local ring with maximal ideal generated by ϖ, hence a DVR with a unique minimal prime. The tensor assertion is obtained from the product description of geometric local and special-fibre components. This is a statement about minimal primes, not a claim that the entire integral ring or entire special fibre is regular or reduced.
proofSteps: Import BCGNT Theorem 2.5.5 for each p-factor from the local lifting-ring sibling. The rank-two BT-specific CN Lemma 5.3.3 is used only for its general algebra argument, supplied by P9.
Use the tame unique-generalization theorem at R and formal smoothness at A. Pass to finite completed tensors after geometric coefficient extension.
acceptance: p>n is retained; no small-prime extrapolation is made.
A generically reduced special fibre is weaker than a globally reduced one.

nodes.title: Unique p-component at characteristic-zero points
nodes.statement: Each characteristic-zero point of Spec R_p lies on a unique irreducible component. Indeed its generic fibre is regular, using Kisin’s crystalline generic-fibre smoothness for every local factor and the corresponding completed-tensor generic regularity. For crystalline weight-zero lifts, the connects hypothesis is used through the common-component interpretation in BCGNT Remark 3.2.2, with the geometric components descended to the chosen E. The component assigned to a given point is independent of frames and further coefficient enlargement. Do not replace this interpretation with potential diagonalizability: the theorem only requires a common component.
proofSteps: Apply crystalline generic smoothness and the completed-tensor regularity comparison. A regular local ring at the point is a domain, giving uniqueness of the component through it.

Use the supplier’s weight-zero base-field crystalline connects comparison to identify the two local point labels; it must be stronger than mere existence of a common component after an unspecified ramified extension.

nodes.title: Residual component transport through distinct types
nodes.statement: Let C be an irreducible component of Spec R_loc^1 and C_p its image component in Spec R_p. Via R_loc^1/ϖ≅R_loc^χ/ϖ for a pairwise-distinct tuple, every generic point of C∩Spec(R_loc^1/ϖ) generalizes to the generic point of the χ-component labelled C_p under the component bijection. Two untwisted components with the same p-label therefore have special generic points generalizing to the same χ-component. The assertion also holds after adjoining the same finite set of patching power-series variables, including existence and codimension one of these special generic points.
proofSteps: Contract a special generic point to the common p-special fibre. Its p-generalization is unique by weight-zero generic reducedness.
Use the distinct-type component projection to lift that p-label to the unique χ-component. Apply the completed tensor and power-series component comparison to retain the same labels after patching.

nodes.title: Adequate crystalline finite-level tower
nodes.statement: For n≥2 and the prepared profile, choose q≥n²f, strictly greater than the dual Selmer dimensions of both residual-identical systems, where f=[F⁺:Q]. For each N≥1 construct Q_N of cardinality q disjoint from S, with q_v≡1 mod p^N, Q_N∩Q_N^c=∅ and underlying rational primes splitting in a fixed imaginary quadratic subfield F₀⊂F. At each v select one eigenvalue α_v of r̄(Frob_v), of generalized-eigenspace multiplicity d_v≥1, and use the (n−d_v,d_v) parahoric and its last-block determinant diamond quotient Δ_v, the p-primary quotient of k(v)ˣ. The deformation condition is MT D_v^1: the distinguished rank-d_v block is inertia-scalar through its diamond character and its complement is unramified. Put Δ_N=∏_{v∈Q_N}Δ_v. There are compatible presentations from R_loc^1[[z_1,…,z_g]] and R_loc^χ[[z_1,…,z_g]] onto the corresponding S-framed global rings, g=q−n²f. Localized dual cohomology C_N,C′_N=RHom_O(RΓ(X_{K₁(Q_N)},O or O(χ⁻¹))_{m_N},O)[−d], d=n²f, is perfect over O[Δ_N], has uniformly bounded perfect representatives after reduction, derived augmentation to C_0,C′_0, and common modulo-ϖ complexes. Surjections R_{S_1,Q_N}→T_N/I_N and R_{S_χ,Q_N}→T′_N/I′_N are O[Δ_N]-linear with one uniform nilpotence bound and common residual action modulo the sum of the two error images. N=0 is the base level with trivial Δ₀. Quotients Δ∞=Z_p^q→Δ_N can be chosen with kernels tending to zero (contained in p^NΔ∞), not merely with bounded ranks.
hypotheses: n≥2; the prepared profile; ζ_p∉F; an allowed all-trivial or everywhere-distinct χ tuple; q chosen as in the statement.
proofSteps: Apply MT Proposition 6.7 and its adequate projector/dual-Selmer argument simultaneously to the two systems, whose special-fibre deformation problems coincide. The scalar-outside hypothesis in the final theorem implies ζ_p∉F; include this certificate in the arithmetic application of the prime theorem.

Use MT §§2–3 block parahoric calculations, not the enormous-image all-distinct-eigenvalue tower. MT Theorem 7.6 gives derived invariants on cohomology; duality gives the stated derived coinvariant augmentation. Good covers and ALS finiteness give uniform bounded perfect models.

Use MT Theorem 7.7 for the selected-block tame Galois condition and CN Theorem 4.2.15 for the crystalline p-condition. Combine them with the WZ.1 Hecke argument and fixed residual coefficient identity. The auxiliary Q and Q^c levels satisfy CN’s parabolic alternatives.

Lift compatible presentations through formal smoothness of the power-series source; use the common residual identification when choosing both sets of lifts. Feed these finite-level data to the existing P8 interface.
acceptance: Only q diamond directions occur, not qn.
The selected α may be repeated, including d_v=n; the zero-size complementary block is allowed.
The proof uses MT §§2–7 and the proof pattern of §8, not Theorem 8.1 under its p>n² Fontaine–Laffaille assumptions.
Require ζ_p∉F for the prime selection; this is supplied by the scalar witness, not by adequacy alone.
